'''Christopher Ike Anigbogu''' (born October 22, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played  [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. As a freshman, he was a key reserve for a Bruins squad that advanced to the Sweet 16 of the [[NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. After the season, he announced that he would declare for the [[2017 NBA draft]].

==Early life==
Anigbogu was born in [[San Diego, California]], to Nigerian parents Chris and Veronica Anigbogu.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ike Anigbogu|website=UCLABruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4743|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170408155817/http://www.uclabruins.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4743|archivedate=April 8, 2017|deadurl=no}}</ref> He attended [[Temescal Canyon High School (Lake Elsinore, California)|Temescal Canyon High]] in [[Lake Elsinore, California|Lake Elsinore]] as a freshman and played on their [[junior varsity team]].<ref name=fowler_03152017>{{cite news|last=Fowler|first=Clay|title=How UCLA built its best roster since Kevin Love joined Russell Westbrook|date=March 15, 2017|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170315/how-ucla-built-its-best-roster-since-kevin-love-joined-russell-westbrook|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/query?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.dailynews.com%2Fsports%2F20170315%2Fhow-ucla-built-its-best-roster-since-kevin-love-joined-russell-westbrook&date=2017-04-09|archivedate=April 9, 2017|deadurl=no}}</ref> The following year, he transferred to [[Centennial High School (Corona, California)|Centennial High]] in [[Corona, California|Corona]], where he was also enrolled in the [[International Baccalaureate]] program.<ref name=whicker_03052017/> A skinny, {{convert|6|ft|7|in|adj=on}} sophomore, he averaged two [[point (basketball)|points]] and 2.5 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game as the Huskies advanced to the state finals.<ref name=fowler_03152017/>

As a junior in 2015, Anigbogu led the team to the state regional finals, where the Huskies lost to [[Chino Hills High School|Chino Hills]], who were led by [[Lonzo Ball]].<ref name=whicker_03052017>{{cite news|last=Whicker |first=Mark |title=UCLA freshman Ike Anigbogu is the last line of defense |date=March 5, 2017 |newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News |url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170305/whicker-ucla-freshman-ike-anigbogu-is-the-last-line-of-defense |archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6pZezKWd5?url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170305/whicker-ucla-freshman-ike-anigbogu-is-the-last-line-of-defense |archivedate=April 8, 2017 |deadurl=no |df= }}</ref> In his senior year, he was limited by injuries and a family emergency.<ref name=pareneti_04162016>{{cite news|last=Pareneti |first=Jeffrey |title=ALL-AREA BOYS BASKETBALL: All-Inland first-team selections |date=April 16, 2016 |newspaper=The Press-Enterprise |url=http://www.pe.com/articles/first-800145-team-players.html |archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6pZkOf0ws?url=http://www.pe.com/articles/first-800145-team-players.html |archivedate=April 8, 2017 |deadurl=no |df= }}</ref> Anigbogu took three weeks off to attend an uncle's funeral in Nigeria.<ref>{{cite news|last=Zink |first=David |title=Huskies Anigbogu learns lesson in appreciation during trip to Nigeria |date=January 12, 2016 |newspaper=The Press-Enterprise |url=http://www.pe.com/articles/anigbogu-791533-basketball-family.html |archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6pZkmAnLH?url=http://www.pe.com/articles/anigbogu-791533-basketball-family.html |archivedate=April 8, 2017 |deadurl=no |df= }}</ref> During the playoffs, he was limited by an injured knee. For the season, the Huskies were 20–5 when Anigbogu played. He finished with averages of 19 points, 11 rebounds and 3 [[block (basketball)|blocks]].<ref name=pareneti_04162016/>

==College career==
Ranked nationally as a consensus top-50 [[college recruiting|recruit]] in the 2016 Class according to [[ESPN]]. Anigbogu attended the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), where he was part of a Bruins freshmen class that included more heralded five-star players Ball and [[T. J. Leaf]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Hines |first=Travis |title=UCLA freshman to miss 4-6 weeks with knee injury |date=October 25, 2016 |work=College Basketball Talk |url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2016/10/25/ucla-freshman-to-miss-4-6-weeks-with-knee-injury/ |archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6pZi2Z1o8?url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2016/10/25/ucla-freshman-to-miss-4-6-weeks-with-knee-injury/ |archivedate=April 8, 2017 |deadurl=no |df= }}</ref>  Anigbogu and Leaf had played on the same [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team, the Compton Magic, who had also been coached by UCLA assistant [[David Grace (basketball)|David Grace]].<ref name=fowler_03152017/> The newcomers were expected to help turn around a program that [[2015–16 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|a year earlier]] had suffered its fourth losing season in the previous 68 years.<ref name=fowler_03252017>{{cite news|last=Fowler|first=Clay|title=Thrilling ride made UCLA basketball’s season-ending loss sting|date=March 25, 2017|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20170325/thrilling-ride-made-ucla-basketballs-season-ending-loss-sting|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/query?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.dailynews.com%2Fsports%2F20170325%2Fthrilling-ride-made-ucla-basketballs-season-ending-loss-sting&date=2017-04-09|archivedate=April 9, 2017|deadurl=no}}</ref>
